edges.description: Connective tissue laxity is associated with hip dislocation in reported ALDH18A1-ADCL cases.
Connective tissue involvement is associated with joint contractures in dominant ALDH18A1 cutis laxa.
A single molecularly confirmed case expands the connective-tissue phenotype to severe cervical instability with cord compression after minor trauma.
The proposed tissue-level branch is associated with cranial vessel tortuosity, but its intermediate mechanism is unknown.
Developmental growth involvement can include prenatal intrauterine growth retardation.
Developmental involvement includes prenatal or postnatal growth delay.
Neurodevelopmental involvement is associated with hypotonia.
Reduced head circumference has been reported in an ALDH18A1-ADCL case, although it is not a defining feature of the dominant disorder.
Neurodevelopmental involvement includes psychomotor and global developmental delay.
Neuroimaging in dominant ALDH18A1 cutis laxa can show cerebral white matter signal abnormality.
Progressive lower-limb hyperreflexia and spasticity are reported within the mitochondrial proline-synthesis disorder spectrum.
Current syndrome-level synthesis identifies a thin corpus callosum as a recurrent ADCL neuroimaging finding.
Ventricular and extra-axial CSF-space enlargement has been documented in an imaged ADCL patient.
Ocular involvement can be expressed as cataract.
